guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.title: Turn Wedding Photos Into a GIF or Slideshow
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.desc: Set the right frame count, duration and canvas size for a wedding photo animation, and avoid the file sizes that break messaging apps.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.lead: An animated GIF is a sequence of still frames, so every extra frame adds weight. Short and small beats long and detailed.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.f2v: Six to twelve images keeps the file shareable
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.f3v: 600–800 px wide is enough for messaging and social
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.f4v: GIF is limited to 256 colours per frame
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.s1: Pick a single canvas ratio and crop every photo to it before animating, otherwise the sequence jitters. Use a consistent duration, add a short hold on the first and last frames, and avoid crossfades if you need the file small — each blended frame is a new full image. Export once at the final size rather than scaling afterwards.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.s2: GIF remains the most compatible animation format for messaging apps and email, but many platforms now prefer short MP4 or WebM video, which handles photographic colour far better. If guests are mostly on WhatsApp, iMessage or WeChat, check the receiving app's size cap and whether it plays GIFs inline. For a wedding website, a lightweight MP4 usually looks better at a fraction of the bytes.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.s3: The usual failures are a file too large to send, banding in skies and dresses caused by the 256-colour limit, and a first frame that flashes before the loop settles. Do not use a GIF for a full-resolution photo album — it is a highlight format, not an archive. Keep the original stills separate.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.q1: How many photos should a wedding GIF use?
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.a1: Six to twelve is a good range. More frames increase file size without giving viewers time to register each image.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.q2: How long should each photo show?
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.a2: About 0.8 to 1.5 seconds. Hold the first and last frame slightly longer so the loop has a clear start and end.
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.q3: Why do the colours look banded?
guides.wedding-photo-to-gif.a3: GIF supports only 256 colours per frame. Photographic gradients show banding; use MP4 if colour fidelity matters.
